subject: Follow-up: VPC egress, PII retention & on-prem constraints
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: VPC egress, PII retention & on-prem constraints

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap + a small set of clarifying questions so we can size the right Private deployment and map procurement: 

Summary of needs from our notes:
- Private/VPC deployment with strict egress controls (no public outbound).
- PII handling: redaction or tokenization of sensitive fields; access controls on raw inputs.
- Retention: short-lived raw inputs/logs; structured audit logs retained for compliance.
- Optional: on-prem / air-gapped option for final POC or production if required.
- Integration: KMS/HSM for key management, SIEM forwarding for audit logs.

Open questions for your team (short answers appreciated):
1) Exact PII categories (SSNs, Payment card numbers, full names + DOB, etc.) and any fields that must never leave customer storage in raw form?
2) Retention windows required for raw inputs vs. aggregated logs (days/months/years)?
3) Will you allow private peering (VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink) to a Hosted-Private instance, or is fully air-gapped on-prem mandatory?
4) Do you require an HSM/KMS SKU integration (customer-managed keys) and specific vendors (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Gemalto/HSM)?
5) Any procurement firewall rules/approved IP ranges we should know about now?

Attached: redwood-map-template.xlsx (blank MAP we use to track owners and dates).

Next step: Can we confirm a short follow-up on Monday to run through the MAP fields? I can loop in solutions engineer Laura for the technical mapping.

Thanks,
Dev
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinSecure Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC egress, PII retention & on-prem constraints

Thanks Dev — good summary. Answers inline below plus an attached security requirements PDF.

1) PII categories: SSN, full payment card numbers (PAN), government IDs, full name + DOB (sensitive for some product flows). We can provide a field-level list from our schema if that helps.

2) Retention windows:
- Raw request payloads (unredacted): maximum 30 days for debugging only; after that must be purged.
- Full audit logs (authentication events, model selection, token counts): retained 1 year.
- Redacted/hashed artifacts for billing/analytics: retain up to 3 years.

3) Network model: For production we require no outbound internet egress from inference hosts. We prefer two options, in order:
  A) VPC Private deployment with PrivateLink/peered-only endpoints and strict egress rules (NAT disabled).
  B) On-premise air-gapped deployment (no internet), delivered as a containerized appliance.
We are open to a Hosted-Private POC in a peered VPC for initial evaluation but production must be A or B.

4) KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys required. AWS KMS is preferred for cloud; for on-prem we need HSM integration (PKCS#11 compatible).

5) Procurement/firewall: we will provide a CIDR block and approved FQDNs for initial peering. Procurement will need an estimated MRR and a list of IPs for pen test scheduling.

Attached: FinSecure-security-requirements.pdf (redacted legal/security artifact).

Elena Rossi
Security Lead | FinSecure
elena.rossi@finsecure.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC egress, PII retention & on-prem constraints

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed answers and the PDF. Quick technical notes and feasible options from our side: 

Feasibility summary:
- VPC Private deployment (Option A): Fully supported. We can deploy into your VPC via PrivateLink or VPC peering. By default we can disable NAT + public egress on inference instances.
- On-prem / air-gapped (Option B): Supported as a special eng runbook. We deliver a containerized bundle with offline model artifacts. Operational notes: artifact transfer via sealed media or allowed transient outbound to an internal artifact registry under your control.

PII & retention controls:
- We support field-level redaction at inference time (configurable pattern rules) — raw payload retention can be limited to 0–30 days by configuration.
- Audit logs: can be forwarded directly to your SIEM over private peering (syslog over TLS) and/or stored encrypted at rest for 1 year.
- Keys: Customer-managed KMS supported (AWS KMS + external HSM via PKCS#11). We also support Bring-Your-Own-Key for model encryption at rest.

Network & logging specifics we need from you to scope network work and estimate effort: 
- Target VPC CIDR(s) and any required subnets for inference/management.
- If using PrivateLink: which account/region to publish endpoints in.
- SIEM endpoint (FQDN/IP) and authentication method (mutual TLS / token).

I've attached a short note describing three deployment patterns and the operational tradeoffs: redwood-private-deploy-options.pdf. If you can share a simple network diagram (even a screenshot) we can draw a proposed topology and call out specific IPs/ports.

I can own the technical POC for the first two sprints; Karthik can handle the procurement/security checklist and pen test coordination.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199
